method: Each of the 30 cited sources was fetched with WebFetch on 14 Nov 2026 (long filings and Federal Register documents in several offset windows) and every number, date, name and definition sentence in the 104 rows was compared with what the source prints; the five explorer supplies and the two Ondo pages were compared with the live values, which matched the rows to the unit. Where a row states a fact that is not in its own cited source it is a finding even if another source on this ledger supports it, unless the row itself names that other source and I verified it there. Not checked: the full text of the Federal Reserve and FDIC proposals beyond their headers, the on-chain data behind any attestation, and the Business Wire release date, which appears only in the URL id (20260805) and not in the fetched text. Second pass, 14 Nov 2026 (60 new rows: reserve components, legal wrappers and five new players): Each of the 15 cited sources was fetched with WebFetch and every figure, name, date and held-at statement in the 60 rows was compared with the text as printed; PDF tables were re-added to their printed totals, and reports were fetched a second time to search for named custodians, banks and fund managers. Live sources matched the rows exactly on the day (Blockscout total_supply 533063044200 at 4 decimals = 53,306,304.42 MONY; Ondo OUSG as of 13 Nov 2026 and USDY as of 11 Nov 2026). Limits: PDFs were read as extracted text through a summarising fetcher, not as page images; the Business Wire copy of the ICE/OKX release carries its date only in the URL (20260305), which ICE's own copy on ir.theice.com confirms as 'Mar 05, 2026'; the BDO report covers one pooled reserve for all fiat-denominated Tether tokens with no per-token split, so the USDT rows are that pool; and status labels inside claims could be checked only against what the release says. Third pass, 14 Nov 2026 (14 rows from two SEC Form N-MFP3 filings): Fetched both cited N-MFP3 XML documents from sec.gov with WebFetch (the Franklin document in two parts, characters 0-100000 and 100000-167751, through its closing tag; the WisdomTree document whole) and compared every number, date and name in each row with the printed element values, then re-summed the four components of each fund. Filing dates and the presence of later N-MFP3 filings were checked against the two data.sec.gov submissions indexes. Values were read out by the fetch tool's extraction model over two differently worded passes per document, not from a raw byte copy. Fourth pass, 14 Nov 2026 (52 rows: RLUSD, USDe, USDS, PAXG, XAUT, USYC, JLTXX, USTB, SWEEP, DTCC, Mastercard and the FCA): Each of the 19 cited sources was fetched with WebFetch (plus the J.P. Morgan AM CUSIP snapshot cited inside h-usdgo-jltxx and the EDGAR filing index), and every figure, date, name and definition sentence in the 52 rows was compared with the text as printed; the 1,068,017-character N-CSRS was read in eleven 100,000-character windows plus targeted passes on the OnChain fund's statements and notes. Gold values (ounces x US$4,157.41) and the USTB value (on-chain shares x $676,987,663 / 60,015,423.56 = $11.2802280) were recomputed and match to the dollar, and live sources read on 14 Nov 2026 matched exactly (Blockscout XAUT 827,417.63, RLUSD 2,019,899,967.19, USDe 4,909,359,615.97, USDS 5,318,034,118.92, USTB 39,660,945.507784; XRPScan RLUSD 762,824,103.291486; Ripple $2,689.9M and $2,826.5M as of 11/12/2026; Circle $312,976,695.16; Superstate $676,987,663). Limits: text was read through a summarising fetcher, not page images; the Business Wire page prints no date (URL 20251210, matched by a MarketScreener/S&P Capital IQ copy dated 12/10/2025); Circle lists 'BNB', read as BNB Smart Chain; o-ustb-ethereum matches only with the unrounded NAV (at exactly $11.2802 it would be $447,383,398); two 'missing' findings name rows that do not exist and are not counted in rows_with_findings. Passes 5 to 9 (14 Nov 2026) checked batch three, tokenized equities, plus four rows left unchecked after pass 4: 33 rows, then the 14 rows changed after pass 5, the 4 changed after pass 6 and the Nasdaq order row after passes 7 and 8, each by a fresh agent that had not seen the work, against the cited page or its mirror of the company's own release. Two pass-5 findings (Ondo and bStocks amounts shown as None) came from the check file leaving out amounts; the pages state the counted figures. Passes 10 and 11 rechecked the Ondo Stocks and bStocks readings with their amounts included; one clause in the Ondo note that rested on another page was moved to a gap note.

Supported: (1) The issuer, Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited, 'a British Virgin Islands business company', is on the Ondo page. The Chainwire page says 'offered and sold by Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited'. (2) Non-US only: the Ondo page says 'offered only outside the United States and only to eligible non-U.S. persons'; Chainwire says 'eligible non-US persons only'. (3) Tokenized US stocks and ETFs: both pages. (4) 'Previously known as Ondo Global Markets': Ondo page only, 'What is Ondo Stocks (previously known as Ondo Global Markets)?'. (5) 'Held with one or more licensed U.S. custodial broker-dealers' is word for word from Chainwire, which carries Ondo's own PRNewswire release (dateline Aug. 15, 2026; 'Ondo Finance today shared...'; 'About Ondo Finance' boilerplate). (6) 'Ondo names none': neither page names a custodian. Finding: the note is narrower than Ondo's own current page. That page says holdings are 'held with one or more U.S.-registered broker-dealers or U.S.-chartered national trust companies'. It also says the tokens are backed by the stock or ETF '(and cash in transit)'. The note leaves out the trust-company alternative and cash in transit, so its broker-dealer-only wording rests on the Aug 15 release alone.

Supported: (1) Certificates: 'bStocks are designed as a Certificate over select U.S. stocks and ETFs'. (2) Issued by 'BTech Holdings Limited, a Binance group affiliate'. (3) Prospectuses approved by ADGM's FSRA. (4) Backing: 'Each bStock is backed 1:1 by a corresponding underlying share held with a regulated custodian'. (5) Self-custody on BNB Chain: 'self-custody them through BNB Chain-compatible wallets'; 'standard BEP-20 tokens on BNB Chain'. Finding: the phrase 'a regulated custodian the issuer does not name' credits the omission to the wrong entity. The page is Binance's release: its SOURCE line is Binance, its only quote is from Binance's co-CEO, and the issuer, BTech, is not quoted. The page shows only that this release names no custodian. It says nothing about whether the issuer names one, for example in its approved prospectus. The page supports 'the release does not name it'.

Supported: this is a Federal Register document (Vol. 91, No. 55, March 23, 2026), so 'filed' holds. It is Release No. 34-105047, dated March 18, 2026. It approves SR-NASDAQ-2025-072 'as modified by Amendment No. 2'. Eligible securities are limited to 'securities in the Russell 1000 Index at the time the service launches', plus 'any additions to the index thereafter'. Also eligible are 'ETFs that track major indices, such as the S&P 500 index and Nasdaq-100 index'. There is a same-order-book provision, and the method described is 'using DTC to clear and settle trades in token form' under the 'DTC Pilot'. Finding: the definition is in the present tense ('trade', 'DTC clears and settles') and drops two qualifiers. First, the order says the rule 'would become effective once the requisite infrastructure and post-trade settlement services have been established by DTC'. Nasdaq must also give members 30 days' notice. Second, same-book trading applies only if the tokenized share 'must be fungible with, share the same CUSIP number and trading symbol with' its traditional counterpart, and gives the same rights. Smaller point: the order says only 'the service' and never names it, so 'DTC's service' is an inference from the DTC Pilot context.

Supported (Payward release, July 2, 2026): 'xStocks are issued by Backed Assets (JE) Limited (a Jersey private limited company)'. In the disclaimer: 'xStocks are not, nor will they be registered with any local securities regulators'. On xStocks generally: 'backed 1:1 by the underlying shares'. The launch covered '60 of the most recognized US-listed companies and ETFs'. The page gives no outstanding total; it gives only $35B total volume, $12.5B on-chain and about 200,000 holders. Finding: 'give price exposure, not ownership' turns a statement about IPO xStocks into one about all xStocks. The page says this only of IPO xStocks: 'IPO xStocks are tokenized equities providing price exposure only — not direct ownership.' Elsewhere it speaks of 'what tokenized equity ownership delivers'. Smaller point: the page never says the tokens are issued 'under' a base prospectus. It only points readers to 'the Base Prospectus and related Final Terms for xStocks'.

Supported: Release 34-105047 dated March 18, 2026 approves SR-NASDAQ-2025-072 as modified by Amendment No. 2; effective once DTC establishes infrastructure and post-trade settlement services; Russell 1000 at launch plus additions, ETFs tracking major indices; same order book, fungible, same CUSIP and symbol, same rights; DTC Pilot. Findings: (1) 'DTC clears and settles them in token form' drops the qualifier that token settlement is elective, 'per order handling instructions that DTC Eligible Participants may select', with fallback to traditional form if DTC cannot tokenize. (2) '30 days' notice' omits the minimum: order says 'at least 30 calendar days', framed as Nasdaq 'would alert', not a stated rule obligation. (3) Status cash_moved is not supported: the order is an approval and records no money movement.

Supported: date (order dated March 18, 2026), grade filed (SEC order in Federal Register, File No. SR-NASDAQ-2025-072, issued for the Commission by Trading and Markets under delegated authority), status announced/label conditional (effective only once DTC infrastructure exists), title, approval as modified by Amendment No. 2, pilot scope (Russell 1000 at launch plus additions; ETFs tracking major indices), same order book, effectiveness trigger, 30-calendar-day member alert. Missing qualifiers: (1) the definition gives the trading condition as only 'if fungible with them', but the page requires the token to be 'fungible with, shares the same CUSIP number with and trading symbol, and affords ... the same rights' (and says 'only if'); (2) 'participants may select settlement in token form' leaves out that only a 'DTC Eligible Participant' (one eligible for the DTC Pilot) may do so.

The cited page supports the amount ('Ondo Stocks now holds $1.01 billion in total value locked (TVL)'), the 440 figure ('with more than 440 assets available'), the date (dateline 'NEW YORK, Aug. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/', no other as-of), and the title. Grade: Chainwire mirror carrying Ondo's own release text ('Ondo Finance today shared a set of ecosystem milestones', About Ondo section), so 'announced' holds. Unsupported: the clause 'Ondo's Global Markets page still says more than $1 billion, undated' has no support on the cited page. The page mentions Ondo Global Markets only in the disclaimer: 'Ondo Stocks are offered and sold by Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited'. That clause rests on a source the row does not cite.

Overstated: claim says settlement 'works'; release says only 'The findings indicate this is achievable securely and with finality across currencies and jurisdictions' and 'BIS Innovation Hub projects are experimental in nature'. Supported: 27 May 2026; 'convened by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) and the Institute of International Finance (IIF)'; seven central banks; 'more than 40 private sector financial institutions'; 'The Bank of Canada has also joined the project'; real-value testing as next step.
